verified.musicOrders: 2026-09-18 read live on the signed-in player (ABSOLUTE VIDEOGAME, 3904 rows): the player bar's shuffle button carries no testid - it is the [data-testid=player-controls] button whose aria-label holds Shuffle ('Enable Shuffle for <playlist>' off, 'Disable ...' on; a Smart Shuffle label is not plain shuffle); [data-testid=control-button-repeat] carries aria-checked false / true (all) / mixed (one) and cycles on a press. The track list is [data-testid=playlist-tracklist] (aria-rowcount = rows + 1), virtualized ~32 rows at a time; its scroller is the nearest ancestor with its own overflow (NOT main): the reader sweeps 0.6 of a screen a step, waits for the first row's index to change, then fills gaps by estimated position - 3829 distinct ids of 3903 rows in 48 s. Rows: [data-testid=tracklist-row] with a[href^=/track/<id>] and a[href^=/artist/]; the row's button aria-label 'Play <title> by <artist>' plays it in the playlist's context; the row's More options menu holds 'Add to queue'. The now-playing widget names no track id - [data-testid=context-item-info-title] + context-item-info-artist are matched against the list read (trackId on the context). Prism's orders run as a one-ahead queue: play the first row, keep exactly one track added to the queue ahead of the playing one, advance on the widget, queue the next; a stray track (Spotify's own context continuing) is answered by queueing the expected one and pressing Next, at most three times a minute. All five hooks live in the musicTracks script; the other four fields are markers so core knows the hooks exist. 2026-09-18 11:05: the queue takes the collection as a third argument and reads the list itself when the page has lost it (a plain press loads the playlist page afresh, and the page's list went with it while core's cache stood - 'read the list first' at 10:53); an album playing is a collection the order button may act on (core: the page's context counts as listed). 11:08: the page on an album when asked for the playlist - the reader took the album grid still on screen for the playlist's (70 rows, then 'the first track was not found'); the navigation now waits for a NEW grid and a 600 ms settle. 11:12: the first row of a reverse (the playlist's last) was not found - the scroll estimate from row index to pixels was off by the page's header, and 12 tries of half a screen never reached it; findRow now aims by the rendered rows' measured pitch, up to 40 tries. And the driver's stray handling had fired before the first track started (it pressed Next on whatever was playing): the driver acts only once the first track is confirmed. 11:15: a playlist page carries a second track list under it (Recommended, rows indexed 1-30 of its own), and every row on the page counted - at the bottom the reader saw that list instead of the playlist's last rows, so the reverse's first track (row 3904) was never found. Rows are read within the playlist's own grid now. 11:18: the one-ahead queue is gone - the row's Add to queue reported a press but Spotify never played the queued track; it ran off the playlist's end into its Recommended list. Prism's orders now press the NEXT row's own Play as the current track's remaining time reaches 2 s (the widget's position and duration), and press the right row at once should anything else play (six such presses a minute at most); a press stands 2.5 s before the driver judges again. The tail of each track loses up to two seconds; no wrong track plays. 2026-09-19: an append after the order's end (Prism's repeat pass) restarts the driver; a press goes back to the collection's page first when the page has been moved (a person browsing the revealed player). Album pages read the same way: [data-testid=track-list], rows with /track/ links and their own Play (Halo OST, 21 rows, read live). 2026-09-19 (B-244): an order named outright on the collection the page plays starts it over - musicStartOver presses the first row's own Play (in order) or a random row's (shuffle, then the switch), and stands down the Prism driver; a service-order switch stands the driver down too (a true shuffle had kept pressing rows under the service's shuffle). 2026-09-19 (B-245): a newer read aborts the sweep of an older one on the page (a generation number) - an album read had taken the page away from a playlist read still sweeping. 2026-09-19 (B-246): a row press the player did not follow is pressed again, three tries, before the driver moves on; a stray track at the end of the handed list holds for the next window instead of ending the order - one missed press at the 3600th of 3828 had ended a true shuffle on the page while the brain still held 228 tracks. 2026-09-19 (B-247): the widget names one artist of several (Scavenger's Den: Skye Lewin, the row: five names), so the track is matched by title first and the artist only tells twins apart, by any shared name.

notes: §32 music adapter slice: transport is forwarded only on a human press (core pass-through) - never on a timer; a missing/localized control falls through to Spotify's own Media Session handlers. Ad-break signal = two concurrent now-playing ad markers, reported the moment they are seen and withdrawn the moment one drops (2026-09-15, mute fast / cover slow: core mutes on the first report and covers after its own window; the page-side 1 s sustain and the 500 ms tick were most of the two to three seconds of ad the room heard). A MutationObserver on the document runs the tick on the mutation itself; the 250 ms timer stands in. The ad subtitle's 'N of M' rides frame.adInfo's count (2026-09-15): the wall's 30 s clock starting over three times reads as three ads, not one stuck ad. Premium accounts never trip it. On-demand play needs Premium - surfaced in the catalog, not fought. Cross-service lookup (musicLookup) drives the player's own page and matches its English labels (More options, Add to playlist, Go to song radio): English only for now - a player in another language answers with that reason. Play orders (2026-09-18): the page's own shuffle and repeat buttons; Prism's true shuffle and reverse through the playlist page's rows (read once, kept 30 min) and a one-ahead queue.
